correctness.rationale: At \(\theta=a\), the source multiplicative gradient satisfies \(m(a)=0\) and \(m'(a)=ah/c\). Since \(\sigma(0)=1/2\) and \(\operatorname{slog}'(0)=1\), direct differentiation gives \(T'(a)=1-\eta_Ah/2+\eta_Mah/c\). The standard one-dimensional fixed-point theorem yields attraction for absolute derivative below one and repulsion above one. For \(\eta_A=0\) and every \(\theta>a\), both \(m(\theta)\) and its signed logarithm are positive, so the trajectory is strictly increasing. A finite limit would have to be a zero of \(m\), but the only such points are \(0\) and \(a\); therefore the trajectory diverges. The exact limit \(m(\theta)\to2\) yields increment limit \(\eta_M\log3\) and hence \(\theta_k/k\to\eta_M\log3\).

value.rationale: HMGD is presented as a theoretically grounded additive–multiplicative framework, and the source explicitly exposes a pure multiplicative specialization. On the simplest positive strongly convex test family, the signed-log term points in the wrong local direction at a positive minimizer unless additive descent dominates it. The exact inequality \(\eta_M<\eta_Ac/(2a)\), together with the full two-sided local frontier and pure-branch divergence speed, gives a concrete safety rule for parameter selection and clarifies which part of the hybridization supplies stabilization.
